title: Private deployment health failure response and IaC safeguards
creator: Maya Chen
description: Create a structured incident response guide and safe automated remediation for the most common Private (VPC) deployment health-check failures, with accompanying Terraform/IaC safeguards and gating. The outcome should reduce manual toil for on-call, lower mean-time-to-repair for common issues, and ensure we never perform unsafe infra changes without operator approval.
background: Private customers run Redwood in their VPCs or on-prem. We see recurring incidents that are operationally similar: node drain/unready events, agent heartbeat failures to the control plane, inconsistent security group rules after manual edits, expired TLS certs for sidecars, and Terraform drift after out-of-band changes. Current runbooks are fragmented across Confluence pages and ad-hoc Slack threads. We need a consolidated, safety-first response guide plus small automated remediations that can be run by on-call or triggered by alerts with human approval.
goals: 1) Produce a single canonical incident response document for Private health failures. 2) Implement a minimal set of automated remediation actions (reconcile SGs, reapply module state, restart failing agents, rotate certs) gated behind approval. 3) Add Terraform/IaC module checks and 'safety gates' to prevent accidental manual drift. 4) Ship monitoring alerts and tests that exercise the remediations in staging.
acceptance_criteria:
- Documented response for 6 common failure classes with clear operator steps.
- 3 automated remediation scripts integrated as runbook playbooks (CLI callable + optional auto-run with approval).
- Terraform module changes to add 'drift-detection' outputs and a remediation toggle.
- E2E test in staging that simulates node unready and validates remediation reduces MTTR by >40% in test runs.
- Security review completed for any automation that writes infra state.
remediation_flows:
(Each flow below includes triage signals, safe-first remediation, and fallback).

1) Node group: 'kube node NotReady'
- Alerts: high proportion of pods Pending, node status NotReady for >2min.
- Triage: kubectl get nodes -o wide; check cloud provider console for instance termination; check system logs (journalctl -u kubelet).
- Safe remediation script: scripts/reconcile_nodes.sh -> performs (a) cordon/uncordon check, (b) attempts kubelet restart systemctl restart kubelet, (c) reconciles ASG target health via aws autoscaling set-desired-capacity (for AWS).
- Fallback: If instance failing bootstrap >15min, trigger replacement via terraform module: terraform apply -target=module.compute[<id>] (requires manual PR or approval).

2) Control-plane agent heartbeat loss
- Alerts: agent heartbeat missing for >30s.
- Triage: check agent logs /var/log/redwood-agent.log; check TLS handshake errors; check connectivity to broker endpoints.
- Safe remediation: restart agent: sudo systemctl restart redwood-agent; run agent selfcheck: /usr/local/bin/agent-selfcheck --quick.
- Automated remediation option: a Lambda/cron job can run agent-selfcheck and restart service if healthcheck passes; this automation is disabled by default and requires runbook toggle in Terraform variables (automation.enabled = true).

3) Security group / network policy drift (customers edit SGs manually)
- Alerts: failing egress to S3 or to control-plane IPs, healthcheck probes returning connection refused.
- Triage: capture current SG rules and compare to IaC state: aws ec2 describe-security-groups | jq .
- Safe remediation: show plan: terraform plan -target=module.network --out=plan.out; review plan; terraform apply plan.out after approval.
- Automated remediation: a 'drift-detect' job creates a PR with terraform plan output against the infra repo and opens a ticket for operators. Automatic apply is blocked unless a signed approval exists (GitHub approval + Slack ack).

4) TLS cert expiry for sidecars or control-plane endpoints
- Alerts: certificate expiry within 7 days or TLS handshake errors.
- Triage: check cert subject and issuer; verify ACME / Vault status.
- Safe remediation: generate new cert via vault write or acme-renewer; deploy with rolling restart: kubectl rollout restart daemonset/sidecar.
- Automation: certificate rotation script implemented but requires 'rotate-certs --dry-run' and explicit operator approval to write secrets.

5) KV cache corruption / high cache miss causing performance spike
- Alerts: elevated token latency, cache miss ratio > 90%.
- Triage: tail runtime logs for OOM, inspect mem usage.
- Remediation: restart serving processes behind a circuit-breaker; clear local cache files with backup; rehydrate cache from stable warmlayer. Automation optional and rate-limited.
automation_design:
We will implement a small 'remediation controller' CLI and a Slack/GH approval workflow: 
- CLI: /opt/redwood/bin/remediate --case <id> --stage triage|repair|apply. It performs readonly checks by default.
- Approval flow: remediation creates a GitHub PR when infra state changes are required. The PR requires 1 approver from SRE and 1 from Security before apply.
- Safe defaults: all automations run in 'dry-run' mode unless automation.enabled=true in the customer's Terraform variables. Even when enabled, destructive operations require a signed approval token.
terraform_considerations:
- Add outputs: network.current_hash, module.compute.version_tag, last_applied_commit to help detect drift.
- Add variable: automation_remediation_mode = "manual|requested|auto" (default manual).
- Add data source checks: ensure critical SGs and routes are managed. If unmanaged resources are detected, create a remediation PR rather than applying automatically.
- Ensure terraform state locking and remote state hints are present before any automated apply.
- Provide example module: modules/guardrails/main.tf with preflight checks implemented as null_resource local-exec that validate environment before acceptance.
monitoring_alerts:
Proposed alert set for Private: 
- private.node-notready > 2 nodes or >20% of nodes NotReady for 2 minutes (severity P1).
- private.agent-heartbeat-missing > 30s (P1).
- private.network-drift-detected (change detected vs last_applied_commit) (P2).
- private.cert-expiry < 7 days (P1).
- private.cache-miss-ratio > 70% for 5 minutes (P2).
Each alert will attach a remediation runbook link and playbook ID so on-call can run the exact automation script with a single command.
rollout_plan:
Phase 1 (staging): land documentation and scripts; run simulated failure tests in staging cluster and iterate (2 weeks).
Phase 2 (internal beta): enable automation.enabled=requested for a subset of internal customers; monitor and collect operator feedback (3 weeks).
Phase 3 (public): enable as optional opt-in for customers, publish docs and RBAC guidance (2 weeks).
All infra-affecting changes require security review and a runbook walkthrough with SRE before Phases 2/3.
testing_plan:
- Unit tests for remediation scripts.
- Integration tests: terraform plan/apply dry-run against staging with injected drift.
- Chaos testing: schedule node termination events and validate CLI remediation reduces MTTR.
- CI gating: require terraform fmt, validate, and plan outputs included in PRs.
- E2E test: simulate cert expiry and validate rotation flow completes under operator approval.
